why: Both move the same five call sites through the one shared AsyncOpenAI client with equivalent safety, so the decision rests on the improvements — and B's vision work is the same catalog-derived capability fix as A's plus the discovery, proven live, that format_messages hardcodes image/jpeg while OpenManus screenshots are PNG, which Anthropic rejects with a 400; A's branch enables images on Anthropic-served models without that fix and would turn a silent degradation into six retried failures per step while reporting it as a win. B also gates the capability lookup on the runtime actually being active, ships 11 tests for it, measures Flex and cache behaviour rather than reasoning about them (including a counter-result on Anthropic that contradicts ROUTER.md, recorded honestly), and labels spend by LLM config — the dimension this app's per-agent LLM(config_name=...) construction actually makes available — where A settles for the runtime's default file:function label.
A_best: Depth of second-order judgment: provider_timeout set to the deadlines the agent loop already enforces client-side (a client timeout doesn't stop the billed generation), and the catch that claude-sonnet-5 rejects temperature, so mapping the retired 3.7 ids to sonnet-4-6 preserves the examples' temperature=0.0 instead of silently changing sampling — a trap B's cheaper substitution walks into. Also the only engineer to find the browser-use CLI MCP subprocess as a third LLM egress.
B_best: Executing the vision improvement live surfaced the image/jpeg-vs-PNG media-type bug that would have broken every Anthropic vision step, and the fix landed as a properly-scoped LLM property with catalog resolution, a MULTIMODAL_MODELS fallback when Router is off, and 11 new tests — a real bug found by proving the change rather than asserting it.
A_worst: improve/vision-catalog is a module-import-time mutation of MULTIMODAL_MODELS that ignores whether Router is active (so it changes behaviour on the provider path too, unflagged) and ships the jpeg/png defect; its live check apparently used a JPEG pixel rather than the PNG screenshots the browser tool actually produces, so the pass is not evidence for the real path.
B_worst: The host unlock is a hardcoded three-host list, so a deployment whose gitignored config.toml names any other public endpoint moves nothing — A's derive-from-configured-base_url rule covers that case — and the model-map and fallback levers are left as prose proposals rather than applicable branches, with the sonnet-5 temperature incompatibility missed.
